summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK Extraction) gap closure by executing plan 23-08 (WinFsp extraction to crate), then run a security review on the phase code, fix findings, add test coverage, and get PR #352 merged.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 gap closure completed, security issues fixed (Ed25519 zeroization, redundant Zeroizing wrapper), 163 new Rust unit tests added across 3 crates, PR #352 created and multiple rounds of automated review comments resolved. Windows CI build remains partially broken (WinFsp super:: module resolution) and was handed off to a Windows debugging session that fixed it.

repo: The workspace Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] entry must specify default-features = false — the consumer's { workspace = true, default-features = false } alone is insufficient for Cargo to suppress defaults

[patch.crates-io] forces Cargo to resolve the patched crate across the entire workspace regardless of whether any feature activates it, causing vendored Unix-only crates (fuser) to attempt compilation on Windows
cipherbox-fuse uses feature flags: 'fuse' = macOS/Linux FUSE, 'winfsp' = Windows WinFSP; they are mutually exclusive and gate entire platform module trees
All KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields already use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with proper cleanup on logout/unmount — the zeroization pattern is established
generate_ed25519_keypair callers were redundantly wrapping return values in Zeroizing::new() — the double-wrapping was unnecessary after fixing the return type
The fuse crate's platform/windows/* modules use super:: to reference sibling modules within platform/windows/, not the crate-level modules gated on cfg(feature = 'fuse')
IpnsPublishRequest derives Debug, which leaked encrypted IPNS key material in logs before the custom Debug impl was added
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code in both macOS/Linux and Windows operations.rs

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair previously returned bare Vec<u8> for private key — changed to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to prevent key material surviving in freed memory

Root workspace.dependencies entry for cipherbox-fuse needed default-features = false — without this, all workspace members inherited the 'fuse' default feature even with --no-default-features CLI flag
Copy-paste bug: app_version and device_model were being set to device_info.device_id after partial move; needed to extract fields before the move into DeviceEntry
encode_libp2p_public_key used 'as u8' cast on key length which silently truncates values > 255; changed to return Result with proper length validation
Vendored fuser lib.rs wrapped with #[cfg(unix)] include!(lib_impl.rs) pattern to make it a no-op on Windows while preserving all functionality on Unix
? operator on logout path propagated transport errors before best-effort cleanup; changed to match to handle errors gracefully
Temp directory cleanup was happening before unmount, meaning cleanup could fail if mount was still active; moved cleanup after successful unmount on both Linux and macOS

fuser and unicode-normalization must stay in regular [dependencies] (optional) not [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] — feature definitions referencing dep:fuser fail on Windows when the dep is target-gated even when the feature isn't activated

workflow: cargo tree -e features is the definitive tool for diagnosing Cargo feature activation issues — it showed cipherbox-desktop activating cipherbox-fuse 'default' feature despite --no-default-features
When a GSD executor agent disconnects mid-plan, spot-check via git log --oneline to see what was committed, then resume from the bookkeeping steps (SUMMARY.md, STATE.md, ROADMAP.md)
1Password SSH signing failures are transient — retry 2-3 times before escalating; they don't block lint-staged hooks
CI roundtripping for platform-specific build issues (especially Windows cross-compilation) is expensive; teleporting the session to the target platform is faster for deep debugging
cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --features X applies --features to ALL workspace members that have that feature, not just the root package
Cargo [patch.crates-io] resolves patched crates globally even when no dependency activates them — vendored Unix-only crates need explicit platform guards in their source

friction: 1Password SSH agent failed to sign commits repeatedly throughout the session, requiring multiple retries
API connection error disconnected the initial gsd-executor agent mid-plan, requiring manual resume and bookkeeping

Windows CI build required 8+ roundtrips through CI (each ~15-20 min) before the root cause (workspace default-features) was identified — teleporting to Windows at iteration 3-4 would have saved significant time
Cargo workspace feature resolution rules are non-obvious: workspace-level dep definition must carry default-features = false, consumer-level alone is insufficient
[patch.crates-io] cannot be made conditional (no cfg support), forcing invasive changes to vendored fuser source to make it compile as a no-op on Windows
CodeRabbit flagged the same ecies.rs min-size check 3 separate times across 3 review rounds despite being resolved and replied to each time
open_items: Windows WinFsp super:: module resolution issue was fixed in the Windows debugging session but the fix hasn't been reviewed — need to understand what the actual fix was
AES-CTR lacks client-side CID verification after IPFS fetch — an attacker controlling the relay could serve tampered ciphertext; marked as HIGH in security review but not addressed this session
file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs uses ed25519_dalek directly (not generate_ed25519_keypair) and is not Zeroizing-wrapped — secondary key generation path left as-is
build_folder_metadata extracts Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with .to_vec() losing zeroization — spawn_metadata_publish receives plain Vec<u8>; acceptable since it's short-lived but worth revisiting
